characterList.description: A man with short curly brown hair, a bit of a beard and mustache, wearing a white button-down shirt and a lavalier microphone. He is the designer of the new London bus.
characterList.name: Thomas Heatherwick

content_metadata.description: An insightful and detailed look into the design process of the new London bus by Thomas Heatherwick.

qAndA.answer: To use 40% less energy than the existing diesel buses.
qAndA.question: What was the primary goal for the energy efficiency of the new bus?

qAndA.answer: They reintroduced bench seats with a single handrail across the top and developed a textile pattern with a large repeat, minimizing the visual noise created by multiple individual seats.
qAndA.question: How did the designers address the issue of visual clutter inside the bus?

qAndA.answer: The new bus is 3 meters longer than the old Routemaster.
qAndA.question: How does the new bus compare in size to the old Routemaster buses?

qAndA.answer: To minimize the perceived bulkiness of the bus, which is significantly larger than previous models.
qAndA.question: Why did the designers choose a rounded shape for the new bus?

qAndA.answer: To create a visually calming effect, accommodate dirt and wear, and echo the shape of the human body.
qAndA.question: What was the rationale behind the textile pattern on the bus seats?

activities.description: Walking into the museum exhibition of the new London bus
Talking about the design brief for the new bus, emphasizing the need for energy efficiency, reliability, and accessibility

characterInteraction.description: Thomas Heatherwick is the only character in this scene, directly addressing the viewer.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The emphasis on accessibility suggests a shift in design thinking, prioritizing the needs of all Londoners.

narrativeProgression.description: The viewer is visually introduced to the new London bus design through a museum exhibition.
Thomas Heatherwick outlines the key aspects of the design brief, highlighting the importance of energy efficiency, accessibility, and improving the user experience.

props.name: Various museum exhibits, including models of the new bus and its components.

scenes.title: Introduction to the New Routemaster Bus

videoEditingDetails.description: Fade in from black to the museum entrance.
Panning shots of the museum exhibition, highlighting different aspects of the bus design.
Cut to a close-up of Thomas Heatherwick talking about the design brief.

activities.description: Discussing further design considerations for the bus, including the decision to incorporate three doors and two staircases, the challenges of accommodating modern needs, and addressing aesthetic issues.

characterInteraction.description: Thomas Heatherwick continues to address the viewer directly, inviting them to understand the design decisions and their reasoning.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The discussion about aesthetic inconsistencies reveals how a lack of consistent design direction can diminish a city's visual identity.

narrativeProgression.description: The rationale for incorporating three doors and two staircases is explained, highlighting the benefits in terms of efficiency and reliability.
Thomas Heatherwick emphasizes the need to address modern needs and challenges in the bus design, such as wheelchair accessibility and accommodating larger baby buggies.

The discussion turns to the aesthetic challenges of designing a modern bus that still reflects the iconic features of London buses while also addressing the inconsistencies that arose due to a lack of consistent design direction over time.

characterInteraction.description: Thomas Heatherwick continues to address the viewer, inviting them to appreciate the design details and their impact on the bus's overall form and function.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The focus on improved user experience and maximizing views of London suggests a desire to elevate the mundane experience of riding a bus to a more aesthetically enjoyable experience.

characterInteraction.description: Thomas Heatherwick maintains direct communication with the viewer, continuing to guide them through the nuanced design aspects of the bus.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The meticulous attention to detail in the textile design emphasizes the commitment to creating a pleasant and aesthetically considered experience for the bus passengers, even amidst the everyday grime and wear of a busy city.

narrativeProgression.description: The rationale behind the rounded shape of the bus is explained, highlighting the goal of reducing its perceived bulkiness, especially when compared to previous models.
Thomas Heatherwick discusses the decision to reintroduce bench seats, highlighting their simplicity and calmness compared to individual bucket seats.

The development of a unique textile pattern for the seats is explored, emphasizing the practicality of incorporating a large repeat that can adapt to the shape of the body and create a more visually calming effect. The need to consider how the bus will look when dirty is also mentioned.

youtube_description:
See more architecture and design movies at http://www.dezeen.com/movies

Thomas Heatherwick talks to Dezeen editor-in-chief Marcus Fairs about redesigning the iconic red double-decker bus for London in this interview filmed by Dezeen at the preview of Heatherwick Studio: Designing the Extraordinary at the V&A museum in London.

In the movie, Heatherwick describes why a second staircase and third door can help the busses stick to a timetable and reveals the best way to disguise traces of kebab smeared on a seat.

The first of the new buses went into service in February, causing a stir with the return of a hop-on-hop-off platform at the back and bands of glass swooping round two stairwells.

See more of Dezeen's architecture and design movies here: http://www.dezeen.com/tag/dezeen-movies/
youtube_title: Thomas Heatherwick on designing a new bus for London
